heroHeadline: KIA-Led Forces Kill 40+ in Kaung Ja Yang Ambush, Sink Two More Vessels as Bhamo River Campaign Grinds On — Day 2,053
heroSubtitle: By Day 2,053 (September 16, 2026), the Bhamo river corridor remained the fiercest active front in Kachin State: KIA-led allied forces ambushed a roughly 100-troop junta reinforcement column near Kaung Ja Yang village on September 12-13, killing more than 40 soldiers (many newly conscripted) and capturing over 30, while a separate ambush near Sawati and Mya Lel sank or damaged six Military Commission vessels the same day, prompting retaliatory junta bombing runs that destroyed roughly half of Kaung Tong village by September 14. A further vessel fleeing Bhamo was sunk near Nat Myet Hna Taung in the Ayeyarwady's second defile on the morning of September 14, and junta shelling near Lu Myan village, Waingmaw Township, wounded two civilians that same day. In Rakhine State, the junta's 'Operation 4926' offensive entered its second week along the Sittwe-Ponnagyun axis, with naval vessels bombarding Mosel and Hsandawshin islands as the Arakan Army continued to repel five junta columns; a September 13 airstrike near Ponnagyun's historic U Raz Mountain pagoda killed two civilians and damaged the site. Elsewhere, a junta jet bombed Bwe Li village in Chin State on September 12 targeting Starlink internet users, a powered paraglider killed six civilians including four women and two children in Minhla Township, Magway Region on September 13, a resistance mine-and-mortar ambush between Monywa and Sagaing killed 20+ junta soldiers the same day, and roughly 80 junta POWs escaped a PDF-Zoland detention facility in Tedim Township that night. On the political track, the junta charged exiled UN Ambassador Kyaw Moe Tun with embezzling state funds on September 12, declaring him a fugitive, drawing a solidarity rally outside the UK Parliament. AAPP's cumulative tally remains 8,335+ confirmed deaths since the 2021 coup, with 31,887 people arrested and 22,663 still detained or unverified; ACLED separately confirmed cumulative conflict deaths across all actors surpassed 100,000 in July. IDPs remain at approximately 5.2 million, with only 26% of the 2025 UN humanitarian appeal funded.
